g.text: (Smaller note: SparkContext (sc) is under the hood, don't worry too much)
Emphasize: Use DataFrames in PySpark 99% of the time!
• Actions = trigger job (show, count, collect, write).
• repartition() (increase) vs coalesce() (decrease, no shuffle usually).
• Use broadcast() for small dimension tables in joins.
Prefer Parquet/ORC over CSV for big data!
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
